stories.summary: Fiona, the beloved Cincinnati Zoo hippo who became a global sensation after surviving a premature birth nearly a decade ago, has died after swallowing a visitor’s knit hat that accidentally ended up in her enclosure, the zoo announced Thursday. The 9-year-old hippo died from complications after veterinarians and animal-care staff made multiple attempts to save her, according to the Associated Press. About 11 days ago, a visitor tossed the knit hat into the air, but a ceiling fan caught it and flung it through a small opening above the enclosure’s viewing windows. “It is with extreme sadness that we share with you the devastating news that Fiona did not make it after multiple attempts from our amazing vets and keeper team to help her through what ended up being a medical emergency,” the zoo said in a statement. This is a developing story.

Grand Theft Auto has been a staple of cable and broadcast TV news since at least the release of Grand Theft Auto III in 2001. I’ve been an adult for all of it; I’ve had a front row seat for two decades of moral panics, parental freakouts, and bizarre political theater. The games and the broader culture’s reaction to them have changed dramatically in that time. In 2001, newscasters worried GTA III was training an army of young men to kill. In 2026, The New York Times earnestly quoted Bell Hooks in its review of GTA VI. For mainstream news, GTA is the ur-video game. The open world that mirrors our own, the prevalence of sex and death, and the increasingly realistic simulations and graphics pointed towards the dream of what a video game could be.
